title: The Atlas of Vilna
premise: In 1941-occupied Vilna, Lior Lockridge works as a battlefield nurse while secretly keeping a ledger of the names the officers' paperwork erases. When a census taker named Marta Vogel asks one question too many, Lior realizes their invisibility has always been borrowed, never owned, and that Marta is hunting the ledger for reasons of her own. As the river ice thaws and the workshop where Lior's father printed forbidden maps faces demolition, Lior must choose between burning the ledger to survive or finishing it and delivering every name to safety before the ice breaks. The book ends with Lior crossing the half-frozen river with the completed atlas, saving the names but losing the workshop, Marta, and the version of themselves that could stay silent.
about_author: Wren Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced-persons records across Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. They write about the small, dangerous acts of record-keeping that history forgets to thank.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. During a routine census visit, Marta Vogel asks not where Lior was born but whom they buried. Lior gives a rehearsed answer, but her pen pauses on the page a beat too long. The chapter establishes the suffocating discipline of Lior's invisibility and ends with the first crack in it: fear that feels almost like being seen.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Omitted
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, moving through the hospital ward at night. We see how the ledger works: names copied from dying men's lips, hidden in the binding of an anatomy text. Emotional beat: tenderness braided with guilt, because recording the dead is both devotion and theft from the living who might be endangered by a single discovered name.

chapters.title: The Workshop on Pylimo Street
chapters.summary: Lior visits the abandoned print shop where their father once engraved maps, now slated for demolition when the ice breaks. Flashback threads show young Lior learning which lines to ink and which to leave blank. Beat: grief sharpening into purpose; the workshop is the only place the ledger can be finished properly.

chapters.title: Marta's Second Visit
chapters.summary: Marta returns, ostensibly to correct a clerical error. Her questions circle closer: does Lior keep accounts, records, lists? Lior lies fluently and hates how good they've become. POV alternates briefly to Marta, revealing she is searching for a ledger she believes exists. Beat: hunter and hunted circling, each mistaking the other's motive.

chapters.title: What the Officers Omit
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A transport of wounded men arrives; three die before giving full names. Lior inventories what the official report leaves out: villages, wives, a boy's real age. Beat: quiet fury. The ledger stops being memorial and becomes accusation, and Lior understands someone will eventually pay for it.

chapters.title: The Ice Reports
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The river begins groaning at night; the demolition order is posted. Lior calculates the timeline: the atlas must be finished and moved before thaw. Introduce Tomas, a teenage courier who offers to help move paper for bread. Beat: fragile hope, and the first admission that Lior cannot do this alone.

chapters.title: Marta's Own Silence
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. In her lodging room we learn why she hunts ledgers: her brother's name vanished from every list after a deportation, and records are the only resurrection she trusts. She suspects Lior but hesitates to report. Beat: her loneliness mirrors Lior's; two people guarding silences that have become prisons.

chapters.title: A Name Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A recovering officer, delirious, recites names of men his unit executed. Lior writes them down, hands shaking. Tomas witnesses this and asks the question no one has dared: whose side is the ledger on? Beat: moral vertigo; the ledger now contains perpetrators as well as victims, and Lior refuses to erase either.

chapters.title: The Anatomy Text
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A spot inspection of the hospital nearly finds the ledger; Lior hides it inside a corpse's effects basket and retrieves it later from the morgue. Beat: terror transmuted into cold clarity. Lior realizes the hiding places are running out faster than the winter is.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Print Shop
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Marta follows Lior to the workshop and confronts them there. Instead of arrest, she makes an offer: her brother's name entered in the ledger, verified, in exchange for her silence. Lior must decide whether a bargain with a census taker is salvation or a leash. Beat: uneasy alliance sealed over the father's dead press.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Moving pages by sledge at night, Tomas reveals he lost his family to a list, not a bullet: a clerk's efficient handwriting. He asks Lior if names can really be saved by ink. Beat: the theme made explicit through the youngest eyes; inheritance as burden passed to a generation that didn't ask for it.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. An old friend from the resistance surfaces, demanding the ledger be burned because any discovery means executions. Lior refuses. The friend leaves a warning: someone else already talked. Beat: isolation deepens; survival is revealed as a debt Lior has been paying with other people's safety all along.

chapters.title: The Denunciation
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta is ordered to produce findings within days. Her superior hints he already knows about a nurse who keeps lists. Torn between protecting her brother's memory and the stranger who guards it, Marta falsifies her first report. Beat: her transformation from instrument to accomplice, knowing there is no way back.

chapters.title: Racing the Thaw
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Daytime temperatures rise; the demolition crew arrives early. Lior, Tomas, and Marta work in shifts printing the final plates: the atlas of names formatted as a map of Vilna, each street holding its dead. Beat: feverish, almost joyful labor; creation under sentence of death.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Soldiers raid the workshop at dawn. Marta stalls them with forged census documents while Lior seals the master plates in oilcloth. Tomas is caught carrying a bundle and doesn't give up the cache. Beat: climax begins; the price of survival comes due in a single morning.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Tomas endures questioning without breaking; Marta is interrogated about her falsified reports and chooses to confess to lesser crimes to shield the greater one. Lior watches from a doorway, unable to intervene. Beat: anguish of witness; love expressed as restraint.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Ice
chapters.summary: Climax. Lior's POV. With hours left, Lior carries the atlas to the river as the ice fractures. The demolition crew fires the workshop behind them. Crossing on cracking floes, Lior nearly drowns, surfacing clutching the oilcloth. Beat: the physical embodiment of the theme; the past literally breaking apart beneath them.

chapters.title: What Was Saved
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, aftermath. On the far bank, Lior takes inventory: the atlas intact, Tomas imprisoned, Marta missing, the workshop ash. Grief and relief arrive together and refuse to separate. Beat: hollowed-out stillness; survival revealed as neither victory nor defeat but a condition to live inside.

chapters.title: Marta's Choice
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Having traded her own position to secure Tomas's release, Marta prepares for deportation herself. She sends Lior one final document: her brother's full record, complete at last. Beat: sacrifice as authorship; she finishes her own entry in the atlas of the omitted.

chapters.title: Deliverance
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior entrusts copies of the atlas to three separate couriers bound for three cities, so no single seizure can erase it. Tomas, freed and changed, asks to learn the trade of remembering. Beat: inheritance fulfilled; the ledger becomes a lineage rather than a secret.

chapters.title: The Empty Workshop
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior walks through the burned ruin of Pylimo Street, salvaging one charred engraving plate: a map with streets but no names, the way officials drew the world. They bury it. Beat: mourning made concrete; letting go of the father's world to carry forward his purpose instead.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep Us Safe
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Lior's POV, twenty years later. An old woman asks Lior, now a quiet archivist in another country, why they never spoke of the war. Lior opens a drawer of copied atlases and answers with a name. Beat: resolution; silence transformed from hiding place into vessel, memory inherited by whoever asks the right question.
